applies_why: The judge text decides STANDS and UNDERDETERMINED grounds, including a dual-sense Isaiah 7:14 line, so the rule governs it.
quote: D5 vs C5 (Isaiah 7:14): UNDERDETERMINED -- C5 bounds Isaiah’s sign with Isaiah 7:16 and 8:3-4 and notes *‘almah* (young woman), while D5 also rests on Matthew 1:23 *parthenos* (virgin); [CR2] G answered the sign rows. GROUND: the near sign and Matthew’s virgin application are both left standing.
rule_words: That a single verse does not state a link or its contrary is never a ground for STANDS or UNDERDETERMINED, for either side. A verse that carries two senses at once is not open. Both senses stand.
room: A verse that carries two senses at once is not open — one reading bars UNDERDETERMINED when a verse has two standing senses; the other allows UNDERDETERMINED when both senses are left standing.
why: The judge labels the Isaiah 7:14 line UNDERDETERMINED because the near sign and Matthew’s virgin application are both left standing, which makes a dual-sense verse open in the very way K-S2 forbids.
